R' Yehuda: forty se'ah in any case
the clause 'but for others forty se'ah' was taught only of a sick man whose emission was normal (hamargil)
but for a sick man whose emission was involuntary (le'onso) -- nine kav [even for others]
anyone [purifying] for others, even a sick man whose emission was involuntary -- not until there are forty se'ah
R' Yehuda's 'forty se'ah in any case' was taught only of [water in] the ground, but in vessels -- no
R' Yehuda's forty se'ah [purifies] even in vessels
for the even-vessels view, R' Yehuda's 'in any case' is [what includes] vessels
for the ground-only view, 'in any case' comes to include drawn water
Rav Pappa: give me [the cup] to bless, for nine kav fell on me
Rava bar Shmuel: rather, give me to bless, for forty se'ah fell on me
Rav Huna: give me to bless, for there is on me neither this nor that
Rav Chama would immerse on the eve of Passover in order to discharge the many their obligation
the halakha follows Rav Chama [on immersing to discharge the many] -- the proposition the stam denies
